src/business/services/MileageService.ts: record() returns `km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM` using a caller-supplied lastServiceKm, so the service-due rule is computed outside the Vehicle model that exports SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM and holds lastServiceKm

src/business/services/MaintenanceService.ts: persistence goes through the VehicleTable/WorkOrderTable gateways (`this.vehicles.row`, `this.orders.write`) and private helpers vehicle()/order() rebuild domain objects; MileageService instead calls `this.prisma.mileage.create` directly and never builds a Vehicle

src/business/services/MaintenanceService.ts close(): `vehicle.returnToService(); ... this.vehicles.write(vehicle.plate, { inService: true, ... })` hardcodes the state instead of reading vehicle.inService, while open() does use `vehicle.inService`
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Both services belong to the fleet domain, but they don't use the same abstraction or boundary. MaintenanceService works through table gateways (VehicleTable, WorkOrderTable) and rebuilds domain objects (Vehicle, WorkOrder) so that the domain methods enforce the rules. MileageService, by contrast, works directly with the Prisma client and doesn't load a Vehicle at all.

MileageService also bypasses its own injected dependency. It receives PrismaService in its constructor, but averageDaily creates a fresh PrismaClient instead.

The service-due rule is also computed inside the service. record() works it out as `km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM`, using a lastServiceKm value the caller passes in, rather than asking the Vehicle model, which owns SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM and lastServiceKm. That puts a copy of the rule outside its natural home. I can't see Vehicle's source, so I'm inferring that it owns this rule from the exported constant and its fields.

In MaintenanceService.close, the code persists a hardcoded `inService: true` instead of `vehicle.inService`. That repeats the result of returnToService() rather than reading the state from the domain object.

Together, these show a split abstraction, a bypass of the module's own dependency, and a rule duplicated outside its owner.

violations.message: averageDaily creates `new PrismaClient()` instead of using the injected PrismaService, which bypasses the module's own dependency.

record() computes the service-due rule itself (`km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM`) from a caller-supplied lastServiceKm instead of delegating to the Vehicle model, so the rule ends up in more than one place.

Uses raw Prisma model access (`this.prisma.mileage.create/findMany`) and never builds a Vehicle, unlike MaintenanceService, which uses the VehicleTable/WorkOrderTable gateways and domain objects. The module's persistence abstraction is inconsistent.
close() writes a hardcoded `inService: true` instead of `vehicle.inService`, repeating the result of Vehicle.returnToService() rather than reading the domain object's state.
